name: ontap-mcp
description: Manage NetApp ONTAP storage clusters from Claude — provision volumes, configure NFS/CIFS, manage snapshots, and more.
long_description:
Runs NetApp's official open-source ONTAP-MCP server (https://github.com/NetApp/ontap-mcp) locally in Docker and bridges it to Claude Desktop.

ONTAP-MCP only speaks Streamable HTTP, not the local stdio protocol Desktop Extensions normally use, so this extension does three things on startup:

1. Writes an `ontap.yaml` credentials file from the settings below into `~/.ontap-mcp-desktop-extension/`.
2. Starts (or restarts) the `ghcr.io/netapp/ontap-mcp` Docker container, publishing it only to `127.0.0.1` on your machine.
3. Bridges Claude Desktop's stdio connection to that local HTTP server using `mcp-remote`.

**Requirements:** Docker Desktop (or another Docker engine) must be installed and running. Nothing is exposed outside your own machine — the container's port is bound to localhost only.

**Security note:** ONTAP-MCP itself has no built-in authentication unless you configure OAuth separately (not covered by this extension). Anything with access to the assistant using this extension can read and, unless Read-Only Mode is left on, modify your ONTAP clusters. Read-Only Mode is on by default.

ontap_address.title: ONTAP Cluster Address
ontap_address.description: Hostname or IP address of your ONTAP cluster management LIF (e.g. 10.193.48.11)

ontap_username.title: ONTAP Username
ontap_username.description: Username used to authenticate to the ONTAP cluster

ontap_password.title: ONTAP Password
ontap_password.description: Password for the ONTAP username above. Stored locally by Claude Desktop and written only to a config file on your own machine, mounted read-only into the local Docker container.

ontap_insecure_tls.title: Skip TLS Certificate Verification
ontap_insecure_tls.description: Enable if your cluster uses a self-signed certificate, which is common for on-prem clusters. Disable to require a valid, trusted certificate.

read_only.title: Read-Only Mode (recommended)
read_only.description: When enabled, only read/list tools are registered — nothing can be created, modified, or deleted on your ONTAP clusters. Turn off only if you want the assistant to make changes.

docker_image.title: Docker Image
docker_image.description: ONTAP-MCP container image and tag to run

local_port.title: Local Port
local_port.description: Local port used to publish the ONTAP-MCP container on 127.0.0.1. Change this if the default is already in use on your machine.

additional_pollers_yaml.title: Additional Clusters (advanced, YAML)
additional_pollers_yaml.description:
Optional. To manage more than one cluster, add extra Pollers entries here in ontap.yaml format, indented as if nested one level under "Pollers:". Example:
cluster2:
  addr: 10.0.0.2
  username: admin
  password: secret
  use_insecure_tls: true
